headline: OCEANA METALS CLOSES SERRA NEGRA DEAL — ASX EXPLORER TAKES 100% OF BRAZIL'S LARGEST CARBONATITE RARE EARTH-NIOBIUM COMPLEX
snippet: Oceana Metals (ASX: OCN) completed its acquisition of Songeo Mineração, owner of the Serra Negra rare earth and niobium project in Minas Gerais, Brazil — a 10-km-wide carbonatite complex in the same Alto Paranaíba Igneous Province as CBMM's world-class Araxá niobium mine. Total consideration is up to US$10.3 million including cash, shares, milestone payments and a 2.5% NSR; a 20,000-metre drill program is planned to define an initial JORC mineral resource at the largest known alkaline carbonatite intrusion in the province.

headline: WARATAH MINERALS GOLDENCLAD FIRST HOLE: 83M AT 1.27 G/T AU FROM 6M — HIGH-GRADE CORE 42M AT 2.23 G/T, 16 ASSAYS STILL DUE
snippet: Waratah Minerals (ASX: WTM) released first-hole results from its Goldenclad gold project, with hole GC001 returning 83 metres at 1.27 g/t gold from just 6 metres depth — including a higher-grade core of 42 metres at 2.23 g/t from 12 metres. Only the top 100 metres of the hole has been assayed with the drill string continuing deeper; 16 further results remain pending from the current campaign, setting up a potential run of results over coming weeks.

headline: US TARIFF THREAT KEEPS COPPER PINNED IN TIGHT RANGE AT LME WEEK OPENING — $14,380 WITH 33% ODDS OF SECTION 232 BY YEAR-END
snippet: Copper traded in a narrow $14,300–$14,500 range at the opening of LME Week 2026, with prediction markets pricing approximately 33% odds of Section 232 copper tariffs by December 31. The tariff floor has prevented a deeper correction despite rising LME warehouse stocks and easing near-term supply concerns, but analysts say the wide band between the tariff-scenario upside ($18,000/t per Macquarie) and a no-tariff correction ($10,000/t) is making it difficult to position aggressively in either direction.

headline: LME WEEK 2026: COPPER TCs AT RECORD NEGATIVE $272/T AND HORMUZ WAR DISRUPTING BASE METALS SUPPLY CHAINS — DEEPEST STRUCTURAL SQUEEZE IN A DECADE
snippet: Fastmarkets' LME Week 2026 analysis documents copper concentrate treatment charges at a record negative $272.20/tonne cif Asia-Pacific — down from negative $69.70 at the start of the year — while Chilean mine output is running 7% below 2025 levels and the Strait of Hormuz closure has disrupted nickel, aluminium and tin flows. Zinc TCs are also at record lows, and Fastmarkets argues this is the most structurally constrained base metals supply environment heading into an LME Week in at least ten years, with implications for junior copper developers sitting on Tier-1 deposits.

headline: GOLD CYCLE MODEL FLASHES NEAR-TERM SELL WHILE LONG-TERM UPTREND HOLDS — HOW TO SIZE MINERS THROUGH THE OCT 27-28 FOMC
snippet: Discovery Alert's proprietary gold cycle model triggered a near-term sell signal on gold miner ETFs on October 17 — the first such reading since June 2026 — while the longer-term trend component remains on a buy. The split signal mirrors setups that have historically preceded 5–8% corrections in gold equities without breaking the primary uptrend; the analysis recommends trimming near-term beta and defining a specific re-entry trigger around $4,200 spot rather than riding through the October 27-28 FOMC decision with full exposure.

headline: NEXMETALS NEARLY TRIPLES SELEBI NORTH COPPER-NICKEL INDICATED RESOURCE — 198% INCREASE TO 8.95MT IN BOTSWANA
snippet: NexMetals Mining (TSX-V/NASDAQ: NEXM) released its Selebi North resource update with an effective date of October 16, 2026, growing the indicated category 198% to 8.95 million tonnes — a near-tripling from the prior estimate. This follows October 1's Selebi Main update which already showed 72% growth to 32.47Mt inferred; the combined Selebi complex in Botswana now carries a materially upgraded resource base to support a revised feasibility study, with the deposit benefiting from existing underground infrastructure from prior operators.

headline: WORLD GOLD COUNCIL: DIGITAL GOLD MARKET COULD TRIPLE TO $160-170 BILLION BY 2031 AS TOKENIZED AND ETF FORMATS CONVERGE
snippet: A World Gold Council report projects the combined digital gold market — encompassing tokenized gold, gold-backed stablecoins and digital ETF structures — could grow from under $60 billion today to $160-170 billion by 2031 as institutional and retail investors in emerging markets adopt gold-linked digital formats. The WGC frames the shift as structurally additional demand on top of existing ETF flows, arguing that digital formats reach investors who cannot access physical gold custody, with implications for the long-term gold price floor.

headline: KIRKLAND LAKE DISCOVERIES HITS 73.86 G/T GOLD OVER 1M AT MIRADO — NORTHERN ONTARIO HIGH-GRADE SHOOT GEOMETRY BEING DEFINED
snippet: Kirkland Lake Discoveries (OTC: KLKLF) reported high-grade gold drill results at its Mirado project in Northern Ontario, including a 1-metre intercept grading 73.86 g/t gold — one of the project's highest-grade single-interval results. The company says the preliminary interpreted footprint is not yet a mineral resource estimate; drilling continues to define the geometry of multiple high-grade shoots that may represent a significant bulk-tonnage halo between them, in a region that hosts some of Canada's most prolific gold producers.

headline: DISCOVERY MINING DOME RESOURCE LOCKED AT 11MOZ INFERRED — TVZ UPDATE BOTH ON TRACK FOR LATE 2026, DRILLING POSITIVE AT BOTH PROJECTS
snippet: Discovery Mining Ltd. (CSE: DSV) confirmed positive drill results from its Dome and TVZ gold projects and said mineral resource estimates for both remain on schedule for late 2026 completion. Dome carries 11.0 million ounces in the inferred category — making it one of the CSE's largest inferred gold resources — with the upcoming MRE expected to upgrade a meaningful portion to the indicated category; TVZ represents a first-time resource that could significantly expand the company's total disclosed ounces.

headline: AURA ENERGY TIRIS Q3 QUARTERLY: DFC LOAN TALKS ACTIVE, FINAL INVESTMENT DECISION TARGETED BEFORE DECEMBER 31 AT $230M MAURITANIAN URANIUM PROJECT
snippet: Aura Energy (ASX/LSE: AEE) released its September 2026 quarterly activities report confirming that a final investment decision at its $230 million Tiris uranium project in Mauritania remains targeted for before December 31, with U.S. International Development Finance Corporation loan negotiations (up to $170 million) ongoing alongside an undisclosed U.S. equity fund and strategic investor. Tiris holds a completed DFS, all major permits, and three uranium offtake agreements; a positive FID in 2026 would make it one of the very few new uranium projects globally to enter construction in the current market cycle.
